nodes.summary: A catenable heap over a type $\alpha$ is a persistent unsorted heap, represented as a join list (catenation tree): it is either the empty heap, an element of $\alpha$ added in front of a catenable heap, or the join of two catenable heaps.
nodes.title: Catenable heap

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ and catenable heap $h$, inserting $x$ into $h$ returns the heap with $x$ added in front of $h$, at cost exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Cost and result of insertion into a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For an element $x$ and a catenable heap $h$, inserting $x$ into $h$ returns the heap with $x$ added in front of $h$ and charges cost $1$, for the one front node it allocates.
nodes.title: Insertion into a catenable heap

nodes.summary: Creating a catenable heap returns the empty heap, at cost $0$.
nodes.title: Cost and result of creating a catenable heap

nodes.summary: The operation that creates a catenable heap returns the empty heap and charges cost $0$, since it allocates no node.
nodes.title: Creating an empty catenable heap

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ and catenable heap $h$, the heap returned by inserting $x$ into $h$ is the heap with $x$ added in front of $h$.
nodes.title: Result of insertion into a catenable heap

nodes.summary: The heap returned by the operation that creates a catenable heap is the empty heap.
nodes.title: Result of creating a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For all catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$, the heap returned by their union is the join of $h_1$ and $h_2$, with $h_1$ as left child and $h_2$ as right child, both unchanged.
nodes.title: Result of the union of catenable heaps

nodes.summary: For every element $a$ and catenable heap $t$, the size of the heap obtained by adding $a$ in front of $t$ is the size of $t$ plus one.
nodes.title: Size of a heap with an element added in front

nodes.summary: The empty catenable heap has size $0$.
nodes.title: The empty catenable heap has size zero

nodes.summary: For every catenable heap $h$, the size of $h$ equals the cardinality of the multiset of its elements.
nodes.title: Size of a catenable heap as a multiset cardinality

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ and catenable heap $h$, the heap returned by inserting $x$ into $h$ has size one more than the size of $h$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a catenable heap increases its size by one

nodes.summary: For catenable heaps $\ell$ and $r$, the size of the join node with left child $\ell$ and right child $r$ is the size of $\ell$ plus the size of $r$.
nodes.title: Size of a catenable heap join

nodes.summary: The heap returned by the operation that creates an empty catenable heap has size $0$.
nodes.title: A newly made catenable heap has size zero

nodes.summary: For catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$, the heap returned by the union of $h_1$ and $h_2$ has size equal to the size of $h_1$ plus the size of $h_2$.
nodes.title: Size of a catenable heap union

nodes.summary: The size of a catenable heap is the length of its left-to-right list of elements, that is, the number of its elements counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Size of a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ and catenable heap $h$, inserting $x$ into $h$ has time cost exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a catenable heap costs one

nodes.summary: The operation that creates an empty catenable heap has time cost $0$.
nodes.title: Creating an empty catenable heap costs nothing

nodes.summary: For all catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$, the union of $h_1$ and $h_2$ has time cost exactly $1$, independently of $h_1$ and $h_2$.
nodes.title: Union of catenable heaps costs one

nodes.summary: For every catenable heap $h$ and list $a$, flattening $h$ from left to right in front of the accumulator $a$ gives the naive left-to-right flattening of $h$ followed by $a$.
nodes.title: Accumulator flattening of a catenable heap

nodes.summary: Given a catenable heap $h$ and a list $s$, the accumulating flattening of $h$ onto $s$ is defined by recursion on $h$: for the empty heap it is $s$; for the heap with an element $x$ added in front of a heap $t$ it is $x$ followed by the accumulating flattening of $t$ onto $s$; for the join of heaps $l$ and $r$ it is the accumulating flattening of $l$ onto the accumulating flattening of $r$ onto $s$.
nodes.title: Accumulating flattening of a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For an element $x$ and a catenable heap $t$, the flattening of the heap with $x$ added in front of $t$ is $x$ followed by the flattening of $t$.
nodes.title: Flattening a front node of a catenable heap

nodes.summary: The flattening of the empty catenable heap is the empty list.
nodes.title: Flattening the empty catenable heap

nodes.summary: For every catenable heap $h$, the flattening of $h$ equals the naive flattening of $h$.
nodes.title: Flattening of a catenable heap equals its naive flattening

nodes.summary: For an element $x$ and a catenable heap $h$, the flattening of the heap returned by inserting $x$ into $h$ is $x$ followed by the flattening of $h$.
nodes.title: Flattening after insertion into a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For catenable heaps $l$ and $r$, the flattening of the join of $l$ and $r$ is the flattening of $l$ followed by the flattening of $r$.
nodes.title: Flattening a join of catenable heaps

nodes.summary: The flattening of the heap returned by the operation that creates a catenable heap is the empty list.
nodes.title: A newly created catenable heap flattens to the empty list

nodes.summary: The naive flattening of a catenable heap is defined by recursion: the empty heap flattens to the empty list, the heap with an element $x$ added in front of a heap $t$ flattens to $x$ followed by the naive flattening of $t$, and the join of heaps $l$ and $r$ flattens to the naive flattening of $l$ followed by that of $r$.
nodes.title: Naive flattening of a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$, the flattening of the heap returned by the union of $h_1$ and $h_2$ is the flattening of $h_1$ followed by the flattening of $h_2$.
nodes.title: Flattening a union of catenable heaps

nodes.summary: The flattening of a catenable heap $h$ is the list of its elements from left to right, computed as the accumulating flattening of $h$ onto the empty list.
nodes.title: Flattening of a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For every element $a$ and every catenable heap $t$, the multiset of elements of the heap obtained by adding $a$ in front of $t$ is the multiset of elements of $t$ with one more copy of $a$.
nodes.title: Multiset of a front node

nodes.summary: The multiset of elements of the empty catenable heap is the empty multiset.
nodes.title: The empty catenable heap has no elements

nodes.summary: For every element $x$ and every catenable heap $h$, the multiset of elements of the heap returned by inserting $x$ into $h$ is the multiset of elements of $h$ with one more copy of $x$.
nodes.title: Insertion adds one copy of the element

nodes.summary: For all catenable heaps $L$ and $R$, the multiset of elements of the join node with left child $L$ and right child $R$ is the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of $L$ and $R$ (multiplicities add).
nodes.title: Multiset of a join node

nodes.summary: The multiset of elements of the heap returned by the make operation is the empty multiset.
nodes.title: A newly made catenable heap has no elements

nodes.summary: For all catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$, the multiset of elements of the heap returned by the union of $h_1$ and $h_2$ is the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of $h_1$ and $h_2$ (multiplicities add).
nodes.title: Union adds the multisets of elements

nodes.summary: The multiset of elements of a catenable heap $h$ is the multiset of the entries of the left-to-right list of elements of $h$.
nodes.title: Multiset of elements of a catenable heap

nodes.summary: For all catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$, the union of $h_1$ and $h_2$ returns the join node whose left child is $h_1$ and whose right child is $h_2$, at cost $1$.
nodes.title: Union allocates one join node

nodes.summary: The union of catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$ allocates one join node, at cost $1$, and returns that join node, whose left child is $h_1$ and whose right child is $h_2$; neither operand is traversed or changed.
nodes.title: Union of catenable heaps

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.

breadcrumbs.label: Lists, stacks, queues and dynamic arrays
